question: What is the cash position and runway?

beat.line: An eleven point four million warrant exercise kept the company afloat — and October added thirteen point eight million more.
beat.headline: +$13.8M
beat.action: Fresh paper coins are taped onto the runway one after another, extending it across the frame.

sources: This was offset by $11.4M raised from warrant exercises (IPO Warrants Tranche 1), which kept the company afloat.
The October 2025 warrant exercise generated $13.8M in cash, which materially strengthened the balance sheet beyond the September 30 snapshot.
prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage. Bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design.
2. One dominant flat block-colour background for the whole shot: lime green. Never a rainbow, never a gradient.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Never a recognisable person's face.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons in cream, black, pale yellow, or the background's contrasting colour. Real paper texture, print dots, small tape pieces.
5. Consistent upper-left light. Small paper-layer shadows only.
6. Everything is flat matte printed paper. No glow, no neon, no bloom, no halos, no luminous edges. Nothing emits light. Not glossy 3D. Not live action.
7. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif, black or cream, printed on paper chips, large, safe margins. English spelling and letterforms accurate and stable. Only the headline text in the copy list, nothing else.
8. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window. One strongest visual focus at a time. No camera shake. Movement starts on the first frame; a small loop continues at the end. No empty frames.
9. Numbers, when specified, are printed complete from their first visible frame. Never counting up, never morphing, never redrawn.
10. No brands, logos, watermarks, or text beyond the copy list.
11. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
12. Identity anchor: rough white torn-paper edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: lime green.
Subjects: fresh paper coins; the runway; tape pieces.
Opens on the runway, carried over from the previous shot, which transforms as the action begins.
Action: Fresh paper coins are taped onto the runway one after another, extending it across the frame.
Ends holding on the extended runway.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "+$13.8M".

COPY LIST: "+$13.8M". Exact strings; nothing else appears in frame.

AUDIO: One English narrator, warm, clear, natural, brisk but unhurried, never an advertising shout. Speak the following line exactly once, word for word, beginning on the first frame: "An eleven point four million warrant exercise kept the company afloat — and October added thirteen point eight million more.". No other dialogue. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects beneath the voice; no music.
expandedPrompt:
integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Cinematic 2D-animated modern editorial paper collage. The scene is set against a dominant, flat, matte lime green block-color background with no gradients. The composition features a black-and-white halftone photographic cutout of a runway, characterized by rough white torn-paper edges and a subtle drop shadow cast from a consistent light source in the upper-left. At the start of the shot, the camera is a Static Shot. A series of black-and-white halftone paper coin cutouts, each with rough white torn-paper edges, enter the frame rapidly with a slight overshoot. One by one, these coins are slapped onto the runway, accompanied by small, flat matte cream-colored paper tape pieces that secure them. This action effectively extends the runway across the lime green space. Simultaneously, a large, extra-bold black sans-serif headline "+$13.8M" appears, printed cleanly on a rectangular cream paper chip with rough white edges, positioned within safe margins. The motion is crisp and refined, settling into a stable reading window. An anonymous paper hand (S1), a black-and-white halftone cutout, briefly enters the frame to place the final coin and tape piece before exiting. The lighting remains flat and matte throughout; there are no glows, neon effects, or 3D gloss. The video ends with the extended runway and the headline holding steady, with a very subtle, slow oscillating loop of the paper elements.

overall_soundscape: A sequence of rhythmic, tactile paper-slap sounds occurs as each coin hits the surface, paired with the short, crisp sticky sound of adhesive tape being pressed down. The environment is otherwise silent, focusing entirely on the physical paper interactions.
